verifiedAgainst: nothing: the quotients were worked out by hand from rules/README.md, Decimals
description: Division in the rule language, for every implementation of it. Each DIV-EXACT and DIV-ROUNDED rule asserts that a quotient is not the value worked out by hand for it, so an engine that divides as rules/README.md says reports every one of them: exactly where the quotient terminates, however many fraction digits that takes, and to 34 fraction digits, half up, where it does not. A rule the engine leaves silent names a quotient it computed differently or not at all. The two DIV-BY-ZERO rules report nothing, because the quotient they read is absent. No rule reads a business term; each names BT-1 because a rule has to name one.

rules.note: The quotient terminates at the 35th fraction digit, one beyond the working precision, and is exact: an engine that rounded every quotient to 34 digits would compute 0.
A divisor of 2 to the power of 3 adds three fraction digits to the 33 of the dividend, and all 36 are kept.
The divisor is 2 to the power of 50, so the quotient needs 50 fraction digits, and it has them.
A quotient that terminates within the working precision is exact as well.
Whether a quotient terminates is decided by the fraction in its lowest terms: 3/12 is 1/4, whose denominator has no prime factor but 2.
The quotient does not terminate: 34 fraction digits, and the 35th, a 3, rounds down.
The rounding matters at the 34th fraction digit: the 35th, a 6, rounds it up, where an engine that cut the digits off would keep a 6.
Half up is away from zero on a negative quotient too.
The working precision counts fraction digits, not significant digits: 34 after the point, 35 digits in all.
34 fraction digits, of which the first three are zeros: the precision is counted from the point, not from the first significant digit.

rules.message: 1 / 0 is {$quotient}, and a division by zero has no quotient.
rules.note: A division by zero is absent, so this rule is not decided and reports nothing. An engine that answered 0 would report DIV-BY-ZERO-NE, and one that answered any other number would report this rule.
